conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that for critically ill, oxygen-dependent COVID-19 patients, corticosteroids like dexamethasone do improve survival, citing strong evidence from large randomized trials and meta-analyses.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
Yes, but with an important nuance: the evidence supports "yes" specifically for the sickest patients—those requiring oxygen or mechanical ventilation—not for all COVID-19 patients.

**The core evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, 2020)** — The landmark UK randomized trial found that dexamethasone (6 mg/day for up to 10 days) reduced 28-day mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring respiratory support. The effect was largest in ventilated patients (~one-third reduction in deaths) and moderate in those needing supplemental oxygen (~one-fifth reduction). https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

2. **WHO REACT Working Group meta-analysis (JAMA, 2020)** — This prospective meta-analysis pooled data from 7 randomized trials (1,703 critically ill COVID-19 patients across 12 countries) and confirmed that systemic corticosteroids were associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality compared to usual care, reinforcing the RECOVERY findings with independent, aggregated trial data. https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279

3. **Corroborating evidence** — Additional analyses, including a critical-care-focused study, further support corticosteroids' survival benefit specifically in critically ill patients. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8818356/

**The key caveat:** Dexamethasone does *not* help—and may even be harmful—in patients with mild disease who don't need oxygen support. The RECOVERY trial specifically found no mortality benefit (and a possible trend toward harm) in this group. This is why guidelines restrict steroid use to hospitalized patients requiring oxygen or ventilation, not all COVID-19 cases.

**Conclusion:** For critically ill, oxygen-dependent COVID-19 patients, corticosteroids like dexamethasone do improve survival—this is one of the most robustly evidence-based COVID-19 treatments, based on large randomized trials and confirmatory meta-analysis.
